name: Today's Report
headline: Case-Shiller's August reading has the San Francisco metro, which includes Alameda County, up 3.4% from a year earlier, ahead of the nation's 2.1%.
teaser: Case-Shiller has the San Francisco metro up 3.4% from a year ago, rates hold at 7.33% before Wednesday's Fed decision, and Microsoft offers buyouts to about 60,000 employees.

rates.source: Mortgage News Daily, the latest for October 27, updated 11:00 AM PT. This report was written before that update, at 7.33% and 6.99%

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Bay Area prices are still climbing. The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller index for August, out this morning, has national home prices up 2.1% from a year earlier, up from 1.9% in July. The San Francisco metro index, which takes in Alameda County, is up 3.4% from a year earlier, though before seasonal adjustment it slipped 0.7% from July, the usual late summer cooling.

Rates and the Fed. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average held at 7.33% Monday and the 15-year is 6.99%, with Tuesday's reading due later today. The Fed announces its rate decision Wednesday at 11 AM Pacific.

What it means for you. Prices here are still rising, about 3.4% a year, but at 7.33% buyers have room to negotiate, so if you are selling, price for today's payment from day one. If you are weighing a buyout from your employer and plan to buy, talk to a lender before you sign: a lump sum is not income, and lenders qualify you on steady income.

Today's count. Inventory thinned. Board wide: 2,578 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,623, with 144 coming soon and 185 brand new. The five city ledger carries 678 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 607 on the market and 71 coming soon, down from 686.

Fremont holds 226 live listings: 181 active, 28 coming soon and 17 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,299,944 at $801 a square foot and a typical listing out 34 days. Hayward carries 198 (from 201), Milpitas 104 (from 103), Newark 89 (from 90) and Union City 61 (from 65). Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $666 a square foot, 284 homes are priced under a million, and 184 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Wednesday is the day to watch. The Fed announces its rate decision at 11 AM Pacific, after raising its target range to 3.75% to 4.00% in September, and futures markets expect a hold this time. Mortgage rates follow the 10-Year Treasury more closely than the Fed's own rate, and the 10-Year closed Monday at 5.00%, unchanged.

Oil eases, metals firm. Brent's December contract settled at $115.81, down 0.78%, and is down 1.55% this morning. Gold rose 0.58% to $4,031 and silver 0.15% to $54.03. The numbers above are Monday's Treasury close, COMEX December gold and silver at the 4 PM ET print, and the ICE December Brent settlement.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Mixed before the Fed. The numbers above are Monday's closes; as of 8:07 AM PT the S&P 500 is up 0.49%, the Dow down 0.03% and the Nasdaq up 0.97%. Wednesday is a double feature: the Fed decides at 11 AM Pacific, and Microsoft reports its quarter the same day.

Microsoft offers buyouts. Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, in the U.S., U.K., Canada and India at level 70 and below, on terms comparable to its standard severance. Sales, some marketing and some engineering teams are left out, and a company spokesperson said artificial intelligence is not driving the program.
